events.boundary: Cultivation and its consequences, from about 12,000 years ago.
events.description: Farming produced surplus, storage, property, hierarchy, writing, money and debt. Time became the calendar of the harvest: the same work in the same field every season. Institutions grew to manage strangers who had to trust each other: temples, granaries, ledgers, kings, courts, and much later banks with double-entry books.

events.boundary: Programmable money: from the 2008 crisis and the first cryptocurrency to smart contracts, decentralized finance and the booms and crashes of 2017 to 2022.
events.description: A ledger nobody owns, that never closes, where code replaces the clerk. It promised to route around the old institutions and instead reproduced most of their temptations at machine speed, in public, around the clock.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

events.boundary: The networked and then pocketed computer, from the public internet of the 1990s to the smartphone and its feeds.
events.description: Information, then attention, then money began to move at the speed of software. A phone in every pocket connected a forager's mind to millions of strangers at once.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

events.boundary: Homo sapiens as mobile foragers, from about 300,000 to about 12,000 years before the present.
events.description: For almost the whole history of the species people lived in bands of a few dozen inside a network of perhaps a hundred and fifty known faces. Trust ran on kinship, reputation and repeated meeting; wealth was what you could carry; a stranger was rare and a threat or a gift. The emotions the protagonist carries (fear of exclusion, hunger for status, the pull of the group, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery) were tuned for this world.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

events.boundary: The global institutional order built mostly after 1944: a world of international money, treaties, clearing systems and multinational banks.
events.description: The global institutions people live inside took shape within roughly the last fifty to eighty years: post-war monetary agreements, the international lenders, card networks, interbank messaging, the floating dollar after 1971. They are younger than many living grandparents, and most people who depend on them have never seen how they work.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

events.boundary: The slow institutions inherited from agrarian and early modern states: the bank, the ledger, the court, the nation state, the working week.
events.description: These are the medieval institutions of E. O. Wilson's phrase: they change on the scale of generations, settle disputes through intermediaries, open at nine and close at five, and remember everything in someone else's book.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.
differentia: Reproduced by guilds, offices, chat servers and crowds.
concepts.label: The band
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.
concepts.label: A key without a map
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.
concepts.label: The peg
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.
differentia: Kieran's teenage skill at games is a way of seeing the world, not only a pastime.
concepts.label: The playing field
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.
differentia: The safety is real but belongs to whoever can end the routine.
concepts.label: Routine as safety
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.
differentia: The vocabulary is agricultural (seed, farm, harvest, stake, pool); the hours are the machine's.
concepts.label: The second agriculture

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.
differentia: Reproduced by guilds, offices, chat servers and crowds.
concepts.label: The band
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.
concepts.label: A key without a map
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.
concepts.label: The peg
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.
differentia: Kieran's teenage skill at games is a way of seeing the world, not only a pastime.
concepts.label: The playing field
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.
differentia: The safety is real but belongs to whoever can end the routine.
concepts.label: Routine as safety
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.
differentia: The vocabulary is agricultural (seed, farm, harvest, stake, pool); the hours are the machine's.
concepts.label: The second agriculture

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.

Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: the spiral.
events.description: Withdrawals from the savings protocol and large sales push the token below a dollar; swaps mint the sister token by the billion; within four days the sister token is worth almost nothing and the stablecoin trades for cents.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

events.boundary: Homo sapiens as mobile foragers, from about 300,000 to about 12,000 years before the present.
events.description: For almost the whole history of the species people lived in bands of a few dozen inside a network of perhaps a hundred and fifty known faces. Trust ran on kinship, reputation and repeated meeting; wealth was what you could carry; a stranger was rare and a threat or a gift. The emotions the protagonist carries (fear of exclusion, hunger for status, the pull of the group, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery) were tuned for this world.

events.boundary: The global institutional order built mostly after 1944: a world of international money, treaties, clearing systems and multinational banks.
events.description: The global institutions people live inside took shape within roughly the last fifty to eighty years: post-war monetary agreements, the international lenders, card networks, interbank messaging, the floating dollar after 1971. They are younger than many living grandparents, and most people who depend on them have never seen how they work.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.
differentia: Reproduced by guilds, offices, chat servers and crowds.
concepts.label: The band
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.

provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.

provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.

events.boundary: The stablecoin and its savings protocol (real in the background, unnamed in the story)
events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. Its savings protocol paid about twenty percent. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less: a spiral that took the peg from a dollar to cents between 9 and 13 May 2022.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: the spiral.
events.description: Withdrawals from the savings protocol and large sales push the token below a dollar; swaps mint the sister token by the billion; within four days the sister token is worth almost nothing and the stablecoin trades for cents.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

events.boundary: Homo sapiens as mobile foragers, from about 300,000 to about 12,000 years before the present.
events.description: For almost the whole history of the species people lived in bands of a few dozen inside a network of perhaps a hundred and fifty known faces. Trust ran on kinship, reputation and repeated meeting; wealth was what you could carry; a stranger was rare and a threat or a gift. The emotions the protagonist carries (fear of exclusion, hunger for status, the pull of the group, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery) were tuned for this world.

events.boundary: The global institutional order built mostly after 1944: a world of international money, treaties, clearing systems and multinational banks.
events.description: The global institutions people live inside took shape within roughly the last fifty to eighty years: post-war monetary agreements, the international lenders, card networks, interbank messaging, the floating dollar after 1971. They are younger than many living grandparents, and most people who depend on them have never seen how they work.

events.boundary: The stablecoin and its savings protocol (real in the background, unnamed in the story)
events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. Its savings protocol paid about twenty percent. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less: a spiral that took the peg from a dollar to cents between 9 and 13 May 2022.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: the spiral.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).

concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.

concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.

concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.

events.boundary: A typical clearing cycle at the Hart.
events.description: The outgoing file is built at ten at night and submitted; overnight the scheme processes it; at seven the exceptions queue shows what failed and why: a closed account, a mismatched name, a fraud flag. events.boundary: The interbank clearing system that the Hart's payments run through

Laura does not know; the next thing she will look at is a mortgage appointment in June. He feels the old band's shame of having led people wrong, although he led nobody, and the child's wish to be no trouble.

events.boundary: The stablecoin and its savings protocol (real in the background, unnamed in the story)
events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. Its savings protocol paid about twenty percent. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less: a spiral that took the peg from a dollar to cents between 9 and 13 May 2022.

events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: the spiral.

concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.

concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.

concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.

events.boundary: Barbara's state in February 2022, when Kieran tells her where the deposit is.
events.description: She has walked with him most months for eighteen months and likes him more than she expected. She thinks everything that is not bitcoin is a casino and the stablecoin a confidence trick with a formula. She believes in adults choosing their own risks and has spent her life refusing to be anyone's mother. Under that, for the first time, is the thought that she gave him the key.

events.boundary: The February 2022 walk: Barbara says it is his choice and nothing more.
events.description: Barbara stops on the track above the long barrow, looks at the barrow for a while, and says: that's yours and Laura's to decide. She says nothing else about it all afternoon. She talks about the men who dragged the stones and about the dog. On the drive home she thinks of three sentences she could have said and says none of them, because she has never been anybody's mother and does not mean to start.

events.boundary: Barbara's card: a white index card with twelve words in her handwriting, and the wallet they open
events.description: Twelve words written in capitals in blue biro, posted to Kieran at the Hart on 1 November 2019 with a note: there is fifty pounds behind these; it is yours; go and look. The words are a recovery phrase for a wallet holding 0.0071 bitcoin. Kieran keeps the card behind his bus pass.

events.boundary: A typical clearing cycle at the Hart.
events.description: The outgoing file is built at ten at night and submitted; overnight the scheme processes it; at seven the exceptions queue shows what failed and why: a closed account, a mismatched name, a fraud flag. Nothing moves at weekends. The failure mode is a file that does not arrive and a day of payments that wait.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.boundary: The interbank clearing system that the Hart's payments run through
events.description: Automated clearing designed for magnetic tape in the late 1960s: files submitted on day one, processed on day two, settled on day three, nothing at weekends. Barbara wrote software for it at a Reading bureau from 1988 to 2013, including the part that holds a payment while it waits.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Britain

events.boundary: The White Hart Building Society (invented): a mutual savings and mortgage society
events.description: Founded in 1868 by railwaymen pooling savings in a White Hart inn to buy houses; now about 1,100 staff, a head office and payments operations in west Swindon. Its day is set by the clearing cut-offs; in 2021 it decides to block payments to several crypto exchanges.

events.boundary: Monday 21 October 2019, 3.40 pm: Kieran's scam-check call to Barbara.
events.description: He reads the script: has anyone contacted you and asked you to move your money, have you been promised returns. She laughs, answers every question and then asks hers: how old is the system he works in, and who could switch it off? He finds he does not know. She asks his name. The payment is released at 4.55.

events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.boundary: Friday 1 November 2019: the letter with the card arrives at the exceptions desk.
events.description: An envelope addressed in capitals to Mr K. Hale, Payments Exceptions, Third Floor, White Hart House. A white card, twelve words, and a note: there is fifty pounds behind these; it is yours; go and look. He must declare gifts from customers. He puts the card in his wallet behind his bus pass.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: Kieran holds everything.
events.description: Four nights at the spare-room desk with the Sharehouse open on one screen and the price on the other. He reads the mechanism again and understands exactly why a run feeds itself. He does not sell at ninety cents, or sixty, or twenty. Laura is on nights; the rota says so. By Friday the deposit is worth about three thousand pounds and falling.

events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: Kieran watches the peg break.
events.description: Four nights at the spare-room desk. The stablecoin slips below a dollar on 9 May; the Sharehouse says it always comes back; the founder's account says he is deploying capital; Kieran reads the mechanism and understands it perfectly. What he does is drawn from cut.kieran.2022.depeg_response.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.boundary: A Sunday in January 2022: Kieran asks and Laura leaves it to him.
events.description: At the kitchen table, with the rota on the fridge behind her, he says he wants to move the deposit somewhere it will earn twenty percent before they buy in the summer. She is marking dates on the calendar and does not look up for long. You're the one who knows about money, she says. Do what you think. He does not explain what a stablecoin is, and she does not ask. By the end of the week the twenty-four thousand pounds is in the savings protocol.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.boundary: January 2022: the house deposit goes into the stablecoin's savings protocol.

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.

Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.
differentia: Reproduced by guilds, offices, chat servers and crowds.
concepts.label: The band
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.
concepts.label: A key without a map
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.
concepts.label: The peg
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.
differentia: Kieran's teenage skill at games is a way of seeing the world, not only a pastime.
concepts.label: The playing field
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.
differentia: The safety is real but belongs to whoever can end the routine.
concepts.label: Routine as safety
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.
differentia: The vocabulary is agricultural (seed, farm, harvest, stake, pool); the hours are the machine's.
concepts.label: The second agriculture

events.boundary: Barbara's state in February 2022, when Kieran tells her where the deposit is.
events.description: She has walked with him most months for eighteen months and likes him more than she expected. She thinks everything that is not bitcoin is a casino and the stablecoin a confidence trick with a formula. She believes in adults choosing their own risks and has spent her life refusing to be anyone's mother. Under that, for the first time, is the thought that she gave him the key.

events.boundary: The February 2022 walk: Barbara says it is his choice and nothing more.
events.description: Barbara stops on the track above the long barrow, looks at the barrow for a while, and says: that's yours and Laura's to decide. She says nothing else about it all afternoon. She talks about the men who dragged the stones and about the dog. On the drive home she thinks of three sentences she could have said and says none of them, because she has never been anybody's mother and does not mean to start.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.
differentia: Reproduced by guilds, offices, chat servers and crowds.
concepts.label: The band
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.
concepts.label: A key without a map
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.
concepts.label: The peg
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.
differentia: Kieran's teenage skill at games is a way of seeing the world, not only a pastime.
concepts.label: The playing field
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.
differentia: The safety is real but belongs to whoever can end the routine.
concepts.label: Routine as safety
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.
differentia: The vocabulary is agricultural (seed, farm, harvest, stake, pool); the hours are the machine's.
concepts.label: The second agriculture

events.description: She has walked with him most months for eighteen months and likes him more than she expected. She thinks everything that is not bitcoin is a casino and the stablecoin a confidence trick with a formula. events.boundary: The February 2022 walk: Barbara says it is his choice and nothing more.
events.description: Barbara stops on the track above the long barrow, looks at the barrow for a while, and says: that's yours and Laura's to decide. She says nothing else about it all afternoon. She talks about the men who dragged the stones and about the dog. On the drive home she thinks of three sentences she could have said and says none of them, because she has never been anybody's mother and does not mean to start.

events.boundary: A typical clearing cycle at the Hart.
events.description: The outgoing file is built at ten at night and submitted; overnight the scheme processes it; at seven the exceptions queue shows what failed and why: a closed account, a mismatched name, a fraud flag. Nothing moves at weekends. The failure mode is a file that does not arrive and a day of payments that wait.

events.boundary: The interbank clearing system that the Hart's payments run through
events.description: Automated clearing designed for magnetic tape in the late 1960s: files submitted on day one, processed on day two, settled on day three, nothing at weekends. Barbara wrote software for it at a Reading bureau from 1988 to 2013, including the part that holds a payment while it waits.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

events.boundary: Kieran's state in early January 2022, before the deposit moves.
events.description: The market is a third down from November; his seventy-one thousand is forty-five on the screen. House prices in Wroughton have risen faster than their deposit. His father has been out of work since July and pretends not to mind. The Sharehouse has spent December saying that the smart money is in safe yield now, twenty percent in a dollar that does not move. He believes he understands risk; what he feels is the old fear of being left behind and the new want to provide. He has not told Laura how much he has made or lost.

events.boundary: Kieran's state on the evening of 9 May 2022, as the peg starts to slip.
events.description: Three hours of sleep a night since the weekend. The deposit is the only money he has that is not already down seventy percent. The Sharehouse is loud and sure: it has always come back, the founder is buying. What he knows about the mechanism depends on what Barbara told him in February. He has not told Laura where the deposit is, or has, depending on January. Leaving now would feel like leaving the band while it is losing.

events.boundary: Kieran's state on 14 May 2022, the morning after.
events.description: The deposit is worth about three thousand pounds and still falling; his own stake is down more than ninety percent from November. He has not slept properly for a week. All that week at the Hart he has taken calls from customers who lost their savings, in the voice he used on Barbara. The Sharehouse has gone from certainty to jokes. Laura does not know; the next thing she will look at is a mortgage appointment in June. He feels the old band's shame of having led people wrong, although he led nobody, and the child's wish to be no trouble.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

events.boundary: The stablecoin and its savings protocol (real in the background, unnamed in the story)
events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less: a spiral that took the peg from a dollar to cents between 9 and 13 May 2022.

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.

events.boundary: Barbara's state in February 2022, when Kieran tells her where the deposit is.
events.description: She has walked with him most months for eighteen months and likes him more than she expected. She thinks everything that is not bitcoin is a casino and the stablecoin a confidence trick with a formula. She believes in adults choosing their own risks and has spent her life refusing to be anyone's mother. Under that, for the first time, is the thought that she gave him the key.

events.boundary: The February 2022 walk: Barbara says it is his choice and nothing more.
events.description: Barbara stops on the track above the long barrow, looks at the barrow for a while, and says: that's yours and Laura's to decide. She says nothing else about it all afternoon. She talks about the men who dragged the stones and about the dog. On the drive home she thinks of three sentences she could have said and says none of them, because she has never been anybody's mother and does not mean to start.

events.boundary: A typical clearing cycle at the Hart.
events.description: The outgoing file is built at ten at night and submitted; overnight the scheme processes it; at seven the exceptions queue shows what failed and why: a closed account, a mismatched name, a fraud flag. Nothing moves at weekends. The failure mode is a file that does not arrive and a day of payments that wait.

events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.boundary: The interbank clearing system that the Hart's payments run through
events.description: Automated clearing designed for magnetic tape in the late 1960s: files submitted on day one, processed on day two, settled on day three, nothing at weekends. Barbara wrote software for it at a Reading bureau from 1988 to 2013, including the part that holds a payment while it waits.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Britain

events.boundary: Monday 21 October 2019, 3.40 pm: Kieran's scam-check call to Barbara.
events.description: He reads the script: has anyone contacted you and asked you to move your money, have you been promised returns. She laughs, answers every question and then asks hers: how old is the system he works in, and who could switch it off? He finds he does not know. She asks his name. The payment is released at 4.55.

events.description: An envelope addressed in capitals to Mr K. Hale, Payments Exceptions, Third Floor, White Hart House. A white card, twelve words, and a note: there is fifty pounds behind these; it is yours; go and look. He must declare gifts from customers. He puts the card in his wallet behind his bus pass.

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: Kieran holds everything.
events.description: Four nights at the spare-room desk with the Sharehouse open on one screen and the price on the other. He reads the mechanism again and understands exactly why a run feeds itself. He does not sell at ninety cents, or sixty, or twenty. Laura is on nights; the rota says so. By Friday the deposit is worth about three thousand pounds and falling.

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: Kieran watches the peg break.

events.boundary: A Sunday in January 2022: Kieran asks and Laura leaves it to him.
events.description: At the kitchen table, with the rota on the fridge behind her, he says he wants to move the deposit somewhere it will earn twenty percent before they buy in the summer. She is marking dates on the calendar and does not look up for long. You're the one who knows about money, she says. Do what you think. He does not explain what a stablecoin is, and she does not ask. By the end of the week the twenty-four thousand pounds is in the savings protocol.

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.
differentia: Reproduced by guilds, offices, chat servers and crowds.
concepts.label: The band
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.
concepts.label: A key without a map
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.
concepts.label: The peg
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.
differentia: Kieran's teenage skill at games is a way of seeing the world, not only a pastime.
concepts.label: The playing field
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.
differentia: The safety is real but belongs to whoever can end the routine.
concepts.label: Routine as safety
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.
differentia: The vocabulary is agricultural (seed, farm, harvest, stake, pool); the hours are the machine's.
concepts.label: The second agriculture

events.boundary: Barbara's state in February 2022, when Kieran tells her where the deposit is.
events.description: She has walked with him most months for eighteen months and likes him more than she expected. She thinks everything that is not bitcoin is a casino and the stablecoin a confidence trick with a formula. She believes in adults choosing their own risks and has spent her life refusing to be anyone's mother. Under that, for the first time, is the thought that she gave him the key.

events.boundary: The February 2022 walk: Barbara says it is his choice and nothing more.
events.description: Barbara stops on the track above the long barrow, looks at the barrow for a while, and says: that's yours and Laura's to decide. She says nothing else about it all afternoon. She talks about the men who dragged the stones and about the dog. On the drive home she thinks of three sentences she could have said and says none of them, because she has never been anybody's mother and does not mean to start.

events.boundary: A typical clearing cycle at the Hart.
events.description: The outgoing file is built at ten at night and submitted; overnight the scheme processes it; at seven the exceptions queue shows what failed and why: a closed account, a mismatched name, a fraud flag. Nothing moves at weekends. The failure mode is a file that does not arrive and a day of payments that wait.

events.boundary: The interbank clearing system that the Hart's payments run through
events.description: Automated clearing designed for magnetic tape in the late 1960s: files submitted on day one, processed on day two, settled on day three, nothing at weekends. events.boundary: The stablecoin and its savings protocol (real in the background, unnamed in the story)
events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. Its savings protocol paid about twenty percent. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less: a spiral that took the peg from a dollar to cents between 9 and 13 May 2022.

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: the spiral.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.
differentia: Reproduced by guilds, offices, chat servers and crowds.
concepts.label: The band
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.
concepts.label: A key without a map
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.
concepts.label: The peg
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.
differentia: Kieran's teenage skill at games is a way of seeing the world, not only a pastime.
concepts.label: The playing field
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.
differentia: The safety is real but belongs to whoever can end the routine.
concepts.label: Routine as safety
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.
differentia: The vocabulary is agricultural (seed, farm, harvest, stake, pool); the hours are the machine's.
concepts.label: The second agriculture

events.boundary: The stablecoin and its savings protocol (real in the background, unnamed in the story)
events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less: a spiral that took the peg from a dollar to cents between 9 and 13 May 2022.

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: the spiral.

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).

concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.

concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.

concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.

events.boundary: August 2022: Barbara goes to Laura herself.
events.description: Something none of the named options held (the remainder was drawn). Barbara, who has never met Laura, takes the bus into Swindon on a weekday while Kieran is at the Hart and knocks on the Wood Street flat. She says who she is. She tells Laura what she did: she gave him a key without a map, and in February she knew how the peg could fail and said nothing, because she has never been anybody's mother. That part is hers, she says; the rest is his; and Laura is allowed to say something. For the first time since June, Laura does.

events.boundary: Barbara's state in February 2022, when Kieran tells her where the deposit is.
events.description: She has walked with him most months for eighteen months and likes him more than she expected. She thinks everything that is not bitcoin is a casino and the stablecoin a confidence trick with a formula. She believes in adults choosing their own risks and has spent her life refusing to be anyone's mother. Under that, for the first time, is the thought that she gave him the key.

events.boundary: The February 2022 walk: Barbara says it is his choice and nothing more.
events.description: Barbara stops on the track above the long barrow, looks at the barrow for a while, and says: that's yours and Laura's to decide. She says nothing else about it all afternoon. She talks about the men who dragged the stones and about the dog. On the drive home she thinks of three sentences she could have said and says none of them, because she has never been anybody's mother and does not mean to start.

events.description: Twelve words written in capitals in blue biro, posted to Kieran at the Hart on 1 November 2019 with a note: there is fifty pounds behind these; it is yours; go and look. events.boundary: A typical clearing cycle at the Hart.
events.description: The outgoing file is built at ten at night and submitted; overnight the scheme processes it; at seven the exceptions queue shows what failed and why: a closed account, a mismatched name, a fraud flag. Nothing moves at weekends. The failure mode is a file that does not arrive and a day of payments that wait.

events.boundary: The interbank clearing system that the Hart's payments run through
events.description: Automated clearing designed for magnetic tape in the late 1960s: files submitted on day one, processed on day two, settled on day three, nothing at weekends. Barbara wrote software for it at a Reading bureau from 1988 to 2013, including the part that holds a payment while it waits.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Britain

events.description: He reads the script: has anyone contacted you and asked you to move your money, have you been promised returns. She laughs, answers every question and then asks hers: how old is the system he works in, and who could switch it off? He finds he does not know. She asks his name. The payment is released at 4.55.

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: Kieran holds everything.

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: Kieran watches the peg break.

events.boundary: A Sunday in January 2022: Kieran asks and Laura leaves it to him.
events.description: At the kitchen table, with the rota on the fridge behind her, he says he wants to move the deposit somewhere it will earn twenty percent before they buy in the summer. She is marking dates on the calendar and does not look up for long. You're the one who knows about money, she says. Do what you think. He does not explain what a stablecoin is, and she does not ask. By the end of the week the twenty-four thousand pounds is in the savings protocol.

events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less: a spiral that took the peg from a dollar to cents between 9 and 13 May 2022.

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.
differentia: Reproduced by guilds, offices, chat servers and crowds.
concepts.label: The band
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.
concepts.label: A key without a map
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.
concepts.label: The peg
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.
differentia: Kieran's teenage skill at games is a way of seeing the world, not only a pastime.
concepts.label: The playing field
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.
differentia: The safety is real but belongs to whoever can end the routine.
concepts.label: Routine as safety
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.
differentia: The vocabulary is agricultural (seed, farm, harvest, stake, pool); the hours are the machine's.
concepts.label: The second agriculture

events.boundary: August 2022: Barbara goes to Laura herself.
events.description: Something none of the named options held (the remainder was drawn). Barbara, who has never met Laura, takes the bus into Swindon on a weekday while Kieran is at the Hart and knocks on the Wood Street flat. She says who she is. She tells Laura what she did: she gave him a key without a map, and in February she knew how the peg could fail and said nothing, because she has never been anybody's mother. That part is hers, she says; the rest is his; and Laura is allowed to say something. For the first time since June, Laura does.

events.boundary: The stablecoin and its savings protocol (real in the background, unnamed in the story)
events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. Its savings protocol paid about twenty percent. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less: a spiral that took the peg from a dollar to cents between 9 and 13 May 2022.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.boundary: 9 to 13 May 2022: the spiral.

events.description: For almost the whole history of the species people lived in bands of a few dozen inside a network of perhaps a hundred and fifty known faces. concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.
differentia: Reproduced by guilds, offices, chat servers and crowds.
concepts.label: The band
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.
concepts.label: A key without a map
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.
concepts.label: The peg
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.
differentia: Kieran's teenage skill at games is a way of seeing the world, not only a pastime.
concepts.label: The playing field
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.
differentia: The safety is real but belongs to whoever can end the routine.
concepts.label: Routine as safety
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.
differentia: The vocabulary is agricultural (seed, farm, harvest, stake, pool); the hours are the machine's.
concepts.label: The second agriculture

events.boundary: August 2022: Barbara goes to Laura herself.
events.description: Something none of the named options held (the remainder was drawn). Barbara, who has never met Laura, takes the bus into Swindon on a weekday while Kieran is at the Hart and knocks on the Wood Street flat. She says who she is. She tells Laura what she did: she gave him a key without a map, and in February she knew how the peg could fail and said nothing, because she has never been anybody's mother. That part is hers, she says; the rest is his; and Laura is allowed to say something. For the first time since June, Laura does.

events.boundary: Barbara's state in February 2022, when Kieran tells her where the deposit is.
events.description: She has walked with him most months for eighteen months and likes him more than she expected. She thinks everything that is not bitcoin is a casino and the stablecoin a confidence trick with a formula. She believes in adults choosing their own risks and has spent her life refusing to be anyone's mother. Under that, for the first time, is the thought that she gave him the key.

She talks about the men who dragged the stones and about the dog. On the drive home she thinks of three sentences she could have said and says none of them, because she has never been anybody's mother and does not mean to start.

events.boundary: A typical clearing cycle at the Hart.
events.description: The outgoing file is built at ten at night and submitted; overnight the scheme processes it; at seven the exceptions queue shows what failed and why: a closed account, a mismatched name, a fraud flag. Nothing moves at weekends. The failure mode is a file that does not arrive and a day of payments that wait.

events.boundary: The interbank clearing system that the Hart's payments run through

events.boundary: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders swapped at once, new sister tokens were minted, its price fell, each swap needed more of them, and the fall fed itself.

concepts.boundary: A small group of known faces, about the size a forager could hold in mind, that shares food, attention and danger and punishes defection.

concepts.boundary: Paleolithic emotions, medieval institutions and godlike technology running at once in one person (E. O. Wilson's phrase; the history as told in Harari's Sapiens).
differentia: Three clocks in one life: the body's, the institution's and the machine's.
concepts.label: The deep-time gap
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Machines that act at planetary scale and machine speed: a ledger nobody owns that never closes, a phone that carries every market into bed.
differentia: Twelve-second blocks, twenty-four hours a day, in public.
concepts.label: Godlike technology
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Access handed over without the understanding or company needed to use it safely.
differentia: Barbara's gift: she verified the key and not the person.

provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Institutions that change over generations and settle through intermediaries: the mutual, the ledger, the court, the working week, the three-day clearing cycle.
differentia: Slow, closing at five, remembering everything in someone else's book.
concepts.label: Medieval institutions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: Fear of exile, hunger for status, loyalty to the band, alarm at sudden loss, delight in discovery: emotions tuned over hundreds of thousands of years of foraging.
differentia: They respond to faces, rank and danger, not to percentages.
concepts.label: Paleolithic emotions
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A promise that holds only while people believe it will hold: a stablecoin's dollar, a bank's deposit, a routine's permanence.
differentia: Its failure is sudden because belief is shared.
concepts.label: The peg
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: The world understood as a game map of which one knew a single corner; past its edges are other players, rules and prizes.

concepts.label: The playing field
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation

concepts.boundary: A life made safe by a repeating schedule owned by an institution.

concepts.boundary: Yield farming as a new domestication: the farmer who checks his fields at three in the morning is kept by the crop, as, in Harari's account, wheat kept its first farmers.
differentia: The vocabulary is agricultural (seed, farm, harvest, stake, pool); the hours are the machine's.

events.boundary: August 2022: Barbara goes to Laura herself.
events.description: Something none of the named options held (the remainder was drawn). Barbara, who has never met Laura, takes the bus into Swindon on a weekday while Kieran is at the Hart and knocks on the Wood Street flat. She says who she is. She tells Laura what she did: she gave him a key without a map, and in February she knew how the peg could fail and said nothing, because she has never been anybody's mother. That part is hers, she says; the rest is his; and Laura is allowed to say something. For the first time since June, Laura does.

events.boundary: The stablecoin and its savings protocol (real in the background, unnamed in the story)
events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. Its savings protocol paid about twenty percent. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less: a spiral that took the peg from a dollar to cents between 9 and 13 May 2022.
